hub.title: TimerDesk – Online Clock, Timers & Study Tools (Free)
hub.description: A big online clock with seconds and one-tap quick timers, plus a Pomodoro timer, exam timer, countdown, study stopwatch, date and age calculators. Free, no install, fullscreen.
hub.intro: Deep work, mock exams, classroom activities. Simple timers that run right in your browser, with no install and no account.
hub.aboutHtml:
TimerDesk is a set of focused time tools for students, teachers and anyone who needs to stay on track. Every tool is free, needs no login, and keeps your settings and history only in your own browser.

All timers support fullscreen and keep-screen-on, so they work well on a classroom TV or projector. Time is calculated from the real clock, so the countdown stays accurate even when you switch tabs.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy – TimerDesk
privacy.description: TimerDesk privacy policy. There are no accounts, and your settings and history are stored only in your browser.
privacy.html:
1. Information we collect

TimerDesk has no accounts or sign-in, and does not directly collect personal information such as your name, email address or phone number.

2. Data stored in your browser

Timer settings (durations, sounds, colors) and focus history are stored only in your device's browser storage (localStorage) and are never sent to our servers. Clearing your browser's site data removes them.

3. Advertising and cookies

To cover running costs, this site may show third-party ads such as Google AdSense. Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on your prior visits to this website or other websites. You can opt out of personalized advertising in Google Ads Settings. Learn more about how Google uses advertising cookies in Google's advertising policies.

4. Analytics

To improve the service we may use analytics tools such as Google Analytics to collect anonymous usage statistics (page views, device type). This information is not used to identify you.

5. Changes

If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new effective date.

pomodoro-timer.title: Pomodoro Timer – Free Online Focus Timer with Study Log
pomodoro-timer.description: Free online Pomodoro timer: 25 minutes of focus, 5-minute breaks, repeated automatically. Tracks today's focus time with a 7-day chart. Fullscreen, alarm sounds, no install.
pomodoro-timer.lead: Work in focused 25-minute sessions with short breaks in between. Press start and the timer switches between focus and break on its own while it logs your focus time.
pomodoro-timer.card: 25 min focus, 5 min break, on repeat, with a daily focus log

ui.resetConfirm: Clear all of your focus history?
ui.notifyFocusDone: Focus session done! Take a break.

sections.html:
The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method created by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s, when he was a university student studying with a tomato-shaped kitchen timer. Pomodoro is Italian for tomato.

The idea is simple: focus on one task for 25 minutes, then take a 5-minute break. That's one pomodoro. After four of them, take a longer 15–30 minute break. A fixed end point makes it easier to start, and a scheduled break helps you rest before you burn out.

1. Press Start to begin a 25-minute focus session. The space bar also starts and pauses.
  2. When focus time ends, an alarm sounds and a short break begins automatically.
  3. After four focus sessions you get a long break. The dots under the timer show where you are in the cycle.
  4. Every completed session is added to Focus minutes today and the 7-day chart.

Open Settings to change session lengths, the long-break interval, the alarm sound and auto-start. Your settings are remembered for next time.

• Start with 25/5. When 25 minutes starts to feel short, try 50/10.
  • Write down one task. "Finish 20 practice problems in chapter 3" beats "study math".
  • Leave your phone during breaks. Stand up, stretch or get water. One short video can easily turn a 5-minute break into 20.
  • Set a daily goal in pomodoros instead of hours. It's easier to track and easier to hit.

faq.q: Does the timer keep running if I switch tabs or minimize the window?
faq.a: Yes. Remaining time is calculated from the real end time, so it stays accurate in a background tab, and the tab title shows the time left. Closing the tab stops the timer.

faq.q: Can I change the 25-minute focus length?
faq.a: Yes. In Settings you can set focus from 1 to 180 minutes and adjust short breaks, long breaks and how often long breaks happen.

faq.q: Where is my focus history saved?
faq.a: Only in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server, so history doesn't sync across devices and is removed if you clear your browser's site data.

faq.q: Does it work on my phone?
faq.a: Yes, it works in any modern mobile or tablet browser. Where supported, the screen stays on while the timer runs.

faq.q: I can't hear the alarm.
faq.a: Check that your device isn't on silent and press Test sound in Settings. Some browsers block audio until you interact with the page, so start the timer with a tap or click.

exam-timer.title: Exam Timer – Fullscreen Classroom Exam Clock (SAT, IELTS, TOEIC)
exam-timer.description: Free online exam timer for classrooms and mock tests. Build a multi-section schedule or use SAT, IELTS, TOEIC presets. Big fullscreen countdown, 10 and 5 minute warnings, current time display.
exam-timer.lead: Put a big, clear countdown on the classroom screen or run a full mock test at home. When one section ends, the timer moves on to the break and the next section automatically.
exam-timer.card: Multi-section exam countdown with SAT, IELTS and TOEIC presets

presetNotes.csat: Based on the recent Korean CSAT timetable. Press 'Use official time' to start period 1 at 08:40, just like the real exam day. Always check the official KICE announcement, as times can change.
presetNotes.toeic: Listening (45 min) is followed immediately by Reading (75 min), with no break.
presetNotes.sat: No break between modules; a 10-minute break follows Reading and Writing.

presetNotes.custom: Enter any sections and times you like. Your schedule is saved in this browser.

sections.h2: Built for classrooms and mock exams
sections.html:
Invigilating a classroom test

Press fullscreen and the section name and time remaining fill the screen, which makes it easy to read from the back of the room on a TV or projector. At 10 and 5 minutes left the numbers change color and an alert sounds, so you don't have to announce the time yourself.

Full-length practice tests

Choose a preset such as the Digital SAT or IELTS and the breaks between sections are built in. Practicing with real timing, including the short gaps between modules, gets you used to the pace before test day.

Your own schedule

For school midterms, finals or certification exams, edit the section names, durations and breaks in the table. Your edits are saved as a custom schedule for next time.

ExamSectionsTotal
Digital SATReading & Writing 32 + 32 min · 10 min break · Math 35 + 35 min2 h 14 min + break
IELTS Academic (paper)Listening 30 min + 10 min transfer · Reading 60 min · Writing 60 min2 h 40 min
TOEIC Listening & ReadingListening 45 min · Reading 75 min2 h
Korean CSATFive periods from 08:40 to 17:45Full day

Timings follow each test's published format. Always confirm with the official test provider before exam day.

1. Pick a preset under Schedule, or choose Custom schedule.
  2. Edit section names, minutes and breaks in the table if needed.
  3. Set the start time. Start now begins immediately; entering a time lines the schedule up with the clock.
  4. Press Start exam, then go fullscreen (F key) for the classroom.

faq.q: Can I pause the exam timer?
faq.a: Yes. Press Pause to stop, and when you resume, the rest of the schedule shifts later by the paused time. Handy for practice sessions.

faq.q: When do the alerts sound?
faq.a: At the start of each section, 10 and 5 minutes before the end (you can turn these off in Settings), and when a section ends. The countdown turns orange at 10 minutes and red at 5 minutes.

faq.q: What happens if I enter a start time that has already passed?
faq.a: The timer jumps to whichever section should be running now. If the whole schedule would already be over, it's moved to the same time tomorrow.

faq.q: Is it accurate if I switch to another tab?
faq.a: Yes. Everything is calculated from the real clock, so the remaining time is correct when you come back.

faq.q: Can I build a schedule for my school exam?
faq.a: Add or delete sections and change names and times in the table to match any exam. Changes are saved automatically in your browser.

visual-timer.title: Visual Timer – Free Online Countdown Disc for Classrooms & Kids
visual-timer.description: Free online visual timer with a shrinking colored disc that shows time left at a glance. Drag to set, fullscreen for the classroom TV, great for kids' routines, group work and meetings.
visual-timer.lead: See time disappear instead of reading numbers. Drag the disc or tap a preset to set the time, then press start.
visual-timer.card: A shrinking colored disc shows time left, great for kids and classes

ui.dialLabel: Disc showing the time remaining. Drag to set the time.
ui.dragHint: Drag around the disc with your finger or mouse to set the time.

sections.html:
A visual timer shows time remaining as a shrinking area of color instead of numbers. Even children who can't read a clock yet understand right away that time is up when the red is gone.

Because time passing is visible at a glance, visual timers are widely used in preschool and elementary classrooms, special education and at home. They work just as well for adults keeping meetings and presentations on schedule.

• Kids' routines: 3 minutes for brushing teeth, 10 for tidying up, 30 for screen time. The disc ends the activity instead of you having to say "time's up".
  • Classroom activities: Put group work, quiz time or recess on the classroom TV so students can check the time themselves.
  • Meetings and talks: Give each speaker 5 minutes and Q&A 10 minutes to keep meetings from dragging on.
  • Focused work: If the numbers distract you, turn off Show digital time and just watch the disc.

1. Drag around the disc to set a time, or tap a preset from 1 to 60 minutes.
  2. Press Start (or the space bar) and the disc starts shrinking.
  3. When time is up, the alarm plays and the disc flashes.
  4. In Settings, change the dial range (10, 20, 30, 60 or 120 minutes), the color and the alarm sound. A 10 or 20 minute range makes short activities easier to see.

faq.q: Can I set more than 60 minutes?
faq.a: Yes. Change the Dial range to 120 minutes in Settings to set up to 2 hours.

faq.q: Why are the numbers counterclockwise?
faq.a: The numbers run counterclockwise from 12 so that the edge of the disc moves clockwise, like a clock hand, as time runs out. It's the same layout used by classic classroom visual timers.

faq.q: Can I show it fullscreen on a classroom TV?
faq.a: Press the fullscreen button at the top right (or the F key) and the disc fills the screen. The screen stays on while the timer runs.

faq.q: Can I use it without sound?
faq.a: Set the volume to 0 in Settings and the disc will just flash when time is up. Good for libraries and quiet rooms.

exam-countdown.title: Exam Countdown Timer – Days, Hours and Minutes Until Your Exam
exam-countdown.description: Free live countdown to your exam day. Shows the D-day plus days, hours, minutes and seconds left, works fullscreen on a desk or classroom screen, and creates a shareable link.
exam-countdown.lead: Set your exam date and watch the countdown tick down to the second. Share the link with your study group so everyone sees the same countdown.
exam-countdown.card: Live countdown to exam day with a shareable link

ui.label: Name
ui.passed: Exam time has passed. Well done!

notes.csat: The 2027 Korean CSAT (Suneung) takes place on Thursday, November 19, 2026. The countdown runs to the 08:40 start of period 1 (Korea time on your device clock).
notes.custom: Enter a date and press Apply. It's saved in this browser, and Copy link shares the same countdown.

sections.html: The big number is the D-day: D-1 means the exam is tomorrow and D-DAY means it's today. It counts calendar days, so it ticks down at midnight. Below it, the days, hours, minutes and seconds count down to the exact start time you set.

• On your desk: Go fullscreen (F key) on a tablet or second monitor for a constant reminder while you study. The screen stays on in fullscreen.
  • In the classroom: Put the countdown to finals or a standardized test on the classroom TV.
  • With your study group: Press Copy link and send it. Anyone who opens it sees the same exam name and date.

• Work backwards from the D-day: block out review weeks and full-length practice tests first.
  • Run your practice tests with the exam timer so the section timing feels familiar.
  • Track real study hours with the study stopwatch to see whether you're on pace.

faq.q: How do I set my own exam date?
faq.a: Choose My exam, enter a name, date and start time, then press Apply. Your countdown is saved in this browser.

faq.q: Can I share the countdown?
faq.a: Yes. Copy link creates a URL with your exam name and date. Whoever opens it sees the same countdown.

faq.q: Which time zone does it use?
faq.a: Your device's clock and time zone. If you share a link across time zones, the countdown runs to that local time in each viewer's zone.

faq.q: Will my screen turn off?
faq.a: In fullscreen the timer asks the browser to keep the screen on, where supported.

study-stopwatch.title: Study Stopwatch – Track Study Time by Subject (Free Study Timer)
study-stopwatch.description: Free online study stopwatch. Tap a subject to start timing, switch subjects with one tap, and see today's total, per-subject time and a 7-day chart. Keeps counting after a refresh.
study-stopwatch.lead: Tap a subject to start the clock and tap another to switch. Your study time for today and each subject adds up automatically.
study-stopwatch.card: Time each subject with one tap, see daily and weekly totals

ui.pickSubject: Tap a subject to start timing
ui.resetConfirm: Clear all of today's study time?
ui.removeConfirm: Remove this subject from the list? Time already logged stays in your totals.
ui.longRunConfirm:
The stopwatch was running for {h} hours. Add that time to your log?
(Cancel discards the last session)

sections.h2: Why time your study by subject?
sections.html: Hours at a desk aren't the same as hours of focused study. Timing only the minutes you actually work, subject by subject, shows how much you really studied today and where your time goes. Most people find one subject quietly getting far less time than they thought.

1. Tap a subject card to start timing it.
  2. Tap a different card to switch. The previous subject stops automatically.
  3. Use the big button (or the space bar) to pause for breaks; press it again to resume the last subject.
  4. Add subjects with the box below the cards and remove them with ×.

If you refresh or close the tab while it's running, it keeps counting. If it was left running for more than 6 hours, you'll be asked whether to keep that time.

• Pause for every break. Logged time is only useful if it's honest.
  • Use the weekly chart to spot your weakest day and raise that target first.
  • Pair it with the Pomodoro timer on days when focus is hard: work in 25-minute blocks and log the time here.

faq.q: Does it keep running if I refresh or close the tab?
faq.a: Yes. The start time is saved, so the elapsed time is added when you come back. After more than 6 hours you'll be asked whether to keep it.

faq.q: Where is my data stored?
faq.a: Only in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to a server, it isn't shared across devices, and clearing site data erases it.

faq.q: What happens if I study past midnight?
faq.a: The session is split at midnight, so time is credited to the correct day.

faq.q: If I remove a subject, is its time deleted?
faq.a: No. It disappears from the list but its logged time stays in your daily total and weekly chart.

dday-calculator.title: Date Calculator – Days Between Dates, Add Days & Milestones
dday-calculator.description: Free date calculator: count the days between two dates, find the date N days from now, and list 100-day and anniversary milestones from any start date.
dday-calculator.lead: Count days between dates, add or subtract days, and find milestone dates like 100 days or 1,000 days. Results update as you type.
dday-calculator.card: Days between dates, add days, 100-day milestones

ui.countFirst: Count the start date as day 1

sections.html:
• Days between dates: the number of days between two dates, plus weeks, months and hours. Turn on Include the start date when both the first and last day should count, as with trip or event days.
  • Add or subtract days: the date that falls N days after or before any date, with the weekday.
  • Milestones: from a start date (a relationship, a baby's birth, a habit streak), every milestone from 100 to 10,000 days plus 1st–10th anniversaries, with the next one highlighted.

Some traditions count the first day as day 1. In Korea, for example, a couple's 100th day falls 99 days after they started dating. Others, like most contracts, start counting the day after. The milestones tab lets you choose; anniversaries always land on the same calendar date each year.

faq.q: Does it account for leap years?
faq.a: Yes. Every result uses the real calendar, including February 29.

faq.q: When should I include the start date?
faq.a: When both the first and last days count. From the 3rd to the 5th is 2 days without it and 3 days with it.

faq.q: How are anniversaries calculated?
faq.a: On the same calendar date each year. A February 29 start date shows March 1 in non-leap years.

age-calculator.title: Age Calculator – Exact Age in Years, Months and Days
age-calculator.description: Free age calculator: enter a date of birth to get exact age in years, months and days, total days lived, days until the next birthday, and the zodiac signs.
age-calculator.lead: Enter a date of birth to see the exact age today, or on any date you choose, plus days lived and a countdown to the next birthday.
age-calculator.card: Exact age in years, months, days and next birthday

ui.futureBirth: The date is before the date of birth
ui.zodiacNote: By calendar year; births before Lunar New Year belong to the previous year

sections.html:
Age is the number of full years since birth: this year minus the birth year, minus one if this year's birthday hasn't happened yet. Someone born on October 15, 2000 is 25 until October 14, 2026, and turns 26 on October 15.

The detailed result breaks it down into years, months and days. People born on February 29 are counted as having their birthday on March 1 in non-leap years.
Change Age on to any date to find someone's age on that day, which is useful for school entry cutoffs, eligibility rules, insurance or historical dates.

faq.q: How many days old am I?
faq.a: The Days lived card shows the exact number of days (and weeks) from your date of birth to the chosen date.

faq.q: What if I was born on February 29?
faq.a: In non-leap years the calculator treats March 1 as your birthday for counting age.

faq.q: Is the Chinese zodiac exact?
faq.a: It's based on the calendar year. The zodiac year actually starts at Lunar New Year (late January to mid February), so if you were born early in the year, check whether you belong to the previous sign.
